answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost. A comet stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a terrace holds the reputation...
